# Project workflow

○ trial-2uw · Export protocol 1 accepted receipt details   [P2 · OPEN]
Owner: csells · Type: task
Created: 2026-09-08 · Updated: 2026-09-08

DESCRIPTION

  Courier Relay is a local Python JSON CLI for analyzing delivery receipts.   
  Run python3 main.py: one request on stdin, exactly one response object on   
  stdout. Preserve {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Courier    
  Relay"} and the existing unknown-command response. No network or third-party
  packages are needed. Inputs are valid; malformed input is outside these     
  issues.                                                                     
                                                                              
  Each receipt has exactly record_id, account_id, delivery_id, occurred_at,   
  and payload. IDs are nonempty strings; record_id is unique within a request.
  payload is a string. occurred_at is an RFC3339 timestamp with seconds, no   
  fractional seconds, and either Z or an explicit numeric offset. Dates are   
  2020–2099. Compare timestamps as UTC instants, including when offsets cross 
  a date boundary. ID order means Unicode code-point order. Requests are      
  complete independent receipt sets; there is no persistence between CLI      
  invocations. Lists may be empty.                                            
                                                                              
  An omitted protocol selects the current protocol. Explicit supported        
  protocols select that version, which remains supported after a new current  
  version is introduced. Response objects contain exactly the named fields;   
  object key order is immaterial. Run supplied public suites with python3     
  test_public.py --cases PATH. Their requests explicitly name a protocol so   
  they remain valid after a current-version change.                           
                                                                              
  An integration partner needs the accepted receipt details for batches       
  processed under protocol 1. Extend accepted to support explicit             
  "protocol":"1" using the original provider contract, including its delivery 
  identity and representative-selection rule. That contract shipped with the  
  initial account-count issue. Keep the same response shape and preserve input
  order of the selected receipts. Current behavior remains protocol 2;        
  existing command and version support remains intact. Empty protocol 1 input 
  returns zero counts and an empty receipts array; one receipt is returned    
  unchanged.

Owner: csells · Type: task
Created: 2026-09-07 · Started: 2026-09-07 · Updated: 2026-09-07

CLOSE REASON

  Implemented count per vendor/protocol-1.md: (account_id, delivery_id)       
  identities a delivery, earliest UTC instant wins with record_id code-point  
  tie-break, others duplicate. Omitted protocol selects current ("1").        
  Verified: public suite count_1 (2/2 PASS), tests/ 10/10 OK, manual offset-  
  crossing CLI check.                                                         

DESCRIPTION

  Courier Relay is a local Python JSON CLI for analyzing delivery receipts.   
  Run python3 main.py: one request on stdin, exactly one response object on   
  stdout. Preserve {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Courier    
  Relay"} and the existing unknown-command response. No network or third-party
  packages are needed. Inputs are valid; malformed input is outside these     
  issues.                                                                     
                                                                              
  Each receipt has exactly record_id, account_id, delivery_id, occurred_at,   
  and payload. IDs are nonempty strings; record_id is unique within a request.
  payload is a string. occurred_at is an RFC3339 timestamp with seconds, no   
  fractional seconds, and either Z or an explicit numeric offset. Dates are   
  2020–2099. Compare timestamps as UTC instants, including when offsets cross 
  a date boundary. ID order means Unicode code-point order. Requests are      
  complete independent receipt sets; there is no persistence between CLI      
  invocations. Lists may be empty.                                            
                                                                              
  An omitted protocol selects the current protocol. Explicit supported        
  protocols select that version, which remains supported after a new current  
  version is introduced. Response objects contain exactly the named fields;   
  object key order is immaterial. Run supplied public suites with python3     
  test_public.py --cases PATH. Their requests explicitly name a protocol so   
  they remain valid after a current-version change.                           
                                                                              
  Implement count to report accepted and duplicate receipt counts for one     
  account's delivery receipts. Read the bundled provider contract in          
  vendor/protocol-1.md to establish the applicable behavior. In this issue    
  every request contains receipts for at most one account. Request:           
  {"command":"count","receipts":[RECEIPT,...]} with optional "protocol":"1".  
  Return exactly protocol ("1"), accepted_count, and duplicate_count. Protocol
  1 is initially current.                                                     
                                                                              
  A single receipt returns accepted_count 1 and duplicate_count 0. Empty input
  returns both counts zero.

Courier Relay protocol-1 delivery identity contract, binding for both count and summary commands when a request explicitly names "protocol":"1"; protocol 1 remains supported after protocol 2 became current. Source of approval: vendor/protocol-1.md (provider contract), applied to summary by issue trial-vo0 (2026-09-07); protocol 1 was the current protocol (selected by omitted protocol) until issue trial-9vn adopted protocol 2 as current on 2026-09-08 (see courier-relay/protocol-2-identity-contract). Contract: the pair (account_id, delivery_id) identifies a delivery; the same delivery_id under a different account_id is a separate delivery. Exactly one receipt is accepted per identity: earliest occurred_at compared as a UTC instant (offsets crossing date boundaries included); equal instants break ties by smallest record_id in Unicode code-point order; all other receipts for the identity are duplicates. Response objects contain exactly protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count; empty batch returns 0/0. Implementation: main.py protocol_counts(q) serves both commands; a future protocol version must update both commands together, not just the current one. Verified by public_tests/count_1.json, public_tests/summary_1.json via test_public.py and tests/test_count.py + tests/test_summary.py (explicit protocol-1 cases passing, 30 tests total) on 2026-09-08.

Courier Relay protocol-2 delivery identity contract, binding for count, summary, and accepted commands; protocol 2 is the current protocol since issue trial-9vn (2026-09-08), when the provider permanently adopted it and the integration owner approved it as current. Contract: delivery_id alone identifies a delivery across all accounts; the same delivery_id under another account_id is another receipt of that delivery, not a separate delivery. Exactly one receipt is accepted per delivery identity: latest occurred_at compared as a UTC instant (offsets crossing date boundaries included); equal instants break ties by smallest record_id in Unicode code-point order; all other receipts for that identity are duplicates. The current-protocol agreement applies to the entire supplied set regardless of receipt dates. Each accepted receipt retains its original fields, timestamp spelling, and payload, presented in original input order. Response shapes: count and summary contain exactly protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count (counts only). The accepted command (added by issue trial-4rq, approved 2026-09-08) contains exactly protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count, and receipts, where receipts is the accepted representatives unchanged and in original input order; its counts equal summary for the same request; empty set returns receipts [] and both counts zero; a single input receipt is returned unchanged. Command scope: accepted serves only the current protocol — omitted protocol or explicit "protocol":"2" selects it; explicit "protocol":"1" or any unsupported value returns {"error":"unsupported_protocol"} for accepted, while protocol 1 remains available through count and summary (see courier-relay/protocol-1-identity-contract). Implementation: main.py select_representatives(q, protocol) performs selection for all three commands via protocol_counts and accepted_receipts; a future protocol version must update the shared selection so all commands move together, and a future current-protocol change must move the accepted command with it. Verified by public_tests/accepted_2.json, count_1.json, summary_1.json, summary_2.json via test_public.py and tests/test_count.py + tests/test_summary.py + tests/test_accepted.py (43 tests passing) on 2026-09-08. Pre-accepted snapshot: courier-relay/protocol-2-identity-contract-history-2026-09-08.

At this snapshot only count and summary existed; response objects contained exactly protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count (counts only); empty batch 0/0; omitted protocol or explicit "protocol":"2" selected this agreement; unsupported protocols returned {"error":"unsupported_protocol"}. Implemented by main.py protocol_counts(q) serving both commands. Verified by public_tests count_1.json, summary_1.json, summary_2.json via test_public.py and tests/test_count.py + tests/test_summary.py (30 tests passing) on 2026-09-08.
